# SetCameraViewMatrix

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Cameras](Blitz3D-Cameras)

</div>


```blitzbasic
SetCameraViewMatrix:Void camera:Int32, matrix:FloatMatrix4x3
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `camera` | In | Int32 | required | Camera handle. |
| `matrix` | In | FloatMatrix4x3 | required | The view matrix, from the world to the camera. |

## Description

Lets a camera look at the world through a view matrix of its own, instead of from where the camera entity is. It stays until [ResetCameraViewMatrix](ResetCameraViewMatrix); moving or turning the camera entity meanwhile does not change the picture. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

The matrix goes from the world to the camera: 4 columns of 3 numbers, the first three are the axes and the fourth is the move. The camera looks down its +Z, with X to the right and Y up, as a camera entity does. Mirrors in the world, [CameraPick](CameraPick), [CameraProject](CameraProject) and culling use the matrix. The entity itself, and what is attached to it, stays where it is.

It is meant for views that an entity can't have, such as a reflected view for a mirror (which has a scale of -1 along one axis).

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
cube = CreateCube()
PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 5
; A camera 3 to the left of the origin: the world moves 3 to the right.
Local view:FloatMatrix4x3 = FloatMatrix4x3(1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 3, 0, 0)
SetCameraViewMatrix camera, view
RenderWorld
Flip
```
